children: WINNIPEG, Manitoba--ICE Futures canola contracts were weaker on Wednesday, taking back some of Thursday's gains with speculative profit-taking a feature.
November canola was up C$16.60 at C$839.10 per tonne, trading well above its major moving averages.
Losses in Chicago soybeans and soyoil contributed to the softer tone in the Canadian oilseed.
Statistics Canada reported canola ending stocks as of July 31, at 1.9 million tonnes. That was up by 19 percent on the year but in line with trade estimates and the five-year average.
The losses in the futures came despite gains in crude oil, which was underpinned by the escalating tensions in the Middle East.
Recent rains across parts of Western Canada Prairies provided some underlying support, as the untimely moisture flooded some fields and raised concerns over potential harvest delays.

Statistics Canada will release its first production estimates for 2026-27 on Sept. 16. Updated U.S. supply/demand estimates from the United States Department of Agriculture will be released on Friday, Sept. 11.
-There were 46,729 contracts traded on Wednesday, which compares with Tuesday when 57,223 contracts changed hands.
Spreading accounted for 21,118 of the contracts traded.
